chapters.timespan: One day: Jaina's pre-dawn crossing and first-light capture (off-page), morning troll sweep, noon stone, afternoon ride, runner arrives, dusk at the Pass, evening cell. The Convocation sits the next day. Season/year not stated.
keyEvents: Before dawn: Jaina crosses the outer ring unfelt; at first light she is found at the split-cap stone on the second ring (reported)
Just before noon: Sylvanas touches the first stone and finds it wrong
Dusk: Sylvanas reaches the Pass, reads Cyndia's report, inspects the gear and map, learns Jaina's name; she enters the cell and says 'Start talking.'

chapters.timespan: Roughly the same night into the next day and dusk. Opens late evening in the cell (same night as chapter 1's dusk) after Jaina sat in the chair 'since before dawn'; ride out at night; dawn at the culvert; sunrise; farms and ambush (prose says 'rooks loud all afternoon'); Millhaven at the last of the light on the day after the arrest. Season: autumn (haws dark red, blackberries over, last leaves on birch).
keyEvents: In the cell, Jaina gives the short version, admits nobody sent her; Sylvanas sets terms; Cyndia pulls the damper wedge; the party leaves the Pass at night
Outside the outer stones the contamination hits Jaina; at dawn at the culvert she goes under and frost forms round her palm; Sylvanas corrects her lines: they close at Millhaven

Farms rotting and empty; ambush at the holly bend by filmed-eyed deer and wolves; Jaina reads the doe and finds contamination in living flesh; the party rides hard and halts above silent Millhaven at dusk
chapters.continuityFlag: The prose has the sun rising during the ride (culvert at dawn, 'this morning' later) and then calls the ambush time afternoon ('rooks had been loud all afternoon') and arrives at Millhaven in 'the last of the light' with the supper hour. The culvert read is morning, ambush afternoon, arrival evening: a full day's ride from dawn to dusk is implied. Keep the Pass-to-Millhaven ride as a long day. Chapter 1's Convocation session sits on this day; Sylvanas is absent, Lor'themar attends in her place.

chapters.timespan: From last light on the day after the arrest (the ride into Millhaven) through the night in the village, first light at the cow way, early morning at the bridge and the party split, then the rest of that day riding south (noon water at a gravel crossing; evening past a living farm). Autumn. Chapter 4 opens two days into the southern ride.
keyEvents: Last light: the party rides into Millhaven; the horses spook; houses swept with no bodies or kill site; Jaina reads the well (mixed crossing result), the inn cellar and the storehouse (loudest, not called the origin); the lane behind the east gardens is found churned by drag marks

Night: Neral finds the hatch under a dragged bed and talks a living child out of the cellar; the girl's account (sweet breath, the sickness order, the glass held to her mam's mouth, feet going past 'up the north road... Up the cow way', 'the newer grain seller'); Jaina checks the horses (clean); Sylvanas holds the warning for first light and sits the gallery

First light: the cow way confirms at least sixty dead went north-northeast toward the ward ring, away from the Pass road; Sylvanas writes the dispatch to Lor'themar; Neral, the fourth ranger and the girl ride north; an old carter arrives from the south, asks about a grain man, and leaves with 'May the stars keep your road'; four ride south over the bridge; noon read: the contamination is wider ahead; evening: a living farm
chapters.chronologyNotes: Sylvanas judges 'five days at the most' from mould on the end-house bowls and has not slept since the night before the troll hollow. The dead walked 'a day and more' ahead. The carter's 'market day' remark is not reconciled with 'five days'. Sylvanas thinks Neral will change saddles at the Pass and the border will be warned 'by tomorrow night'. In one early line Sylvanas recalls riding down the road 'an hour before dusk' (Ch2 had last light).

chapters.timespan: One long day and a night into the next morning: arrival in the sick village on a working morning (before noon), infirmary work through the afternoon, Sylvanas's report at dusk, the granary at dusk, Tam's death in full dark, the shutdown and burning through the night, the ward vigil to before dawn, rain before dawn, departure the next morning. Autumn. Plan: two days' ride south of Millhaven (the prose gives no count).
keyEvents: Late morning: the four riders (Jaina rested, Sylvanas, Cyndia, Lyriel; Neral and the fourth ranger absent) ride into a working village; Brask's spear across the lane; Sylvanas talks him down with Millhaven; Jaina and Lyriel go to Tobin's chapel infirmary with Dickon

Afternoon: Jaina reads and wards the sick (Elsie, Garran, the cooper's boy and wife, Col, Wenna Dunmore), learns Lyriel's one-handed knot, builds the slate and the bread answer; Sylvanas and Cyndia work the granary and bakehouse and find the new man's flour

Dusk: Jaina's report and Cyndia's report converge on 'on purpose'; the party goes into the granary; Tam in the loft with a jar; arrow, frost, shell ward; Jaina reads the built substance; Brask arrives; the cage
Full dark: Tam dies of poison from his collar; Jaina asks for the night shutdown; Brask orders the granary and bakehouse shut and every house's flour burned; Dickon turns the ford cart
Night: Jaina feeds wards round after round; Lyriel rebinds her torn hand; Cyndia brings Mother Haw's oatcakes; Sylvanas reports 'It's burned.'

Before dawn: it rains; dawn: Elsie's fever has broken, Garran unchanged; loft boards (with Jaina's ice) burned; Sylvanas shows the ANDORHAL sacking; names written in Brask's ledger; the party rides out onto the grain road southwest
chapters.chronologyNotes: Garran fell ill 'since before market'; Elsie came in 'this morning' (fainted in the byre yesterday); the cooper's boy hot since yesterday, his mother since the day before; Col came down two days ago; Joss's last load was a fortnight ago; the new man began three months ago. Jaina: Millhaven 'a fortnight ago or a week or however long it had been' (uncertain). The ford cart was sent 'this morning' (day of arrival) and caught that night. Sylvanas sets the deadline at 'cockcrow'; the baker lights his oven 'before light'. The chapter does not repeat the day-count from Millhaven; do not assume a number beyond the plan's 'two days'. The old carter and Neral's party are not mentioned. Next chapter (5): the same four riders on the grain road southwest.

chapters.timespan: About three and a half days, autumn: afternoon after the ford (day 1) through the night of day 3 to dawn of day 4/5. Day 1: afternoon at Corley's depot, sleep in the carters' inn loft. Day 2: stops (miller past Coldwell, hamlet shop, Wick, second depot), the table at a south-road inn by late afternoon, night ride through the river-road wood past the Plough. Day 3: grey dawn at the river depot, the overseer, Brill road north all day to the toll-bar at sunset, back through a second sleepless night. Day 4: first grey at the padlocked depot, stove ash and slips all morning/day, midnight at the carters' lodge at the fork. Day 5: first light, turn south onto the south road.
keyEvents: Afternoon, day after the sick village (they crossed the ford at noon; the dawn rain's water still in the ruts): Corley's crossroads depot; the out-book; short-rate 'own cart' loads from midsummer; Jaina reads four roads from a mile-post; the joint sheet; counts by road; 31 places
Night: loft of the carters' inn across the road; Sylvanas takes the watch twice

Day 2: miller past Coldwell (the cart man bought sacks back yesterday), hamlet shop, Wick (a carter left south before light), second depot (the big depot on the river road breaks the Andorhal loads); at the south-road inn the table: 47 places, 19 in more than one book; brown-coat men: Arthas at Strahnbrad; Sylvanas decides not to stop at the Plough

Night ride through the hazel-and-oak wood; Jaina laughs at Lyriel's 'paid by the loop'; the Plough watered only; grey dawn at the river depot: three swept barns, raked yard, a lit stove; the overseer lies (Brill, Tolliver and Sons); Jaina finds nothing on him
Day 3: Brill road north; causeway; clay hill: no cut ruts after the rain; toll-bar at sunset: no grain on that road for a month; Back; the mare goes down on the causeway at night

Day 4 first grey: the depot padlocked, the house abandoned, the bridge-keeper saw the overseer and wife go south yesterday; the stove ash: 53 slips with Andorhal at one end, Barov on 31, a melted shield seal

Midnight, the carters' lodge at the fork: slips read against Jaina's reads; the staff light leans to the south bend; Ashford corrected; the old carter's wagon recalled; Cyndia reports army wagons; Strahnbrad is pinned into the bench; first light: south onto the bending road under a moving brown smear over the hills
chapters.chronologyNotes: Counting is loose: the prose says 'three days' without count; 'the second night without sleep' is on the Brill road return; the depot's chain padlock and the overseer's flight were 'yesterday, not long after the bells for morning' (the bridge-keeper, said at dawn of day 4: i.e. the overseer fled the same day the party rode north, the party having left him at dawn that day); the rain 'before dawn on the morning they rode out of the village' (day 0) is the rain referred to for the slumped ruts; the toll-keeper's 'a company of the King's foot, a week gone'. Ch5 refers to 'the back end of summer' for the boy's collar placing and midsummer for the first short-rate load.

chapters.timespan: Day 5, morning to the last working hours of the day. Early morning on the south-road climb (a few hours after leaving the fork at first light); late morning to midday at the Strahnbrad camp; the afternoon ride down to the flat; late afternoon at the rise above Andorhal in low gold light.
keyEvents: Morning on the south road climb under mist: the late hitch at the culvert; Jaina assembles the pieces into 'one thing, made in parts' and says to Sylvanas 'It comes in on the wagons and walks out on its own feet'; her fear that the author was trained in Dalaran; the road climbs out of the mist into army dust and smoke

Strahnbrad: the party is held at a hedge gap by a sergeant; Sylvanas hands Jaina the sheet; Arthas arrives, believes the warning, and chooses the Garrow-farm war; Sylvanas calls the decision; Arthas never takes the paper; Jaina's internment-camp memory; Jaina concedes 'You were right'; they decline food and go for Andorhal

Afternoon: the flat fills with carts; a granary tally-man gives directions to Captain Havel at the market-gate militia post and says 'May the stars keep your road'; Sylvanas, a second time, finds the farewell wrong; Jaina read nothing off him

Late afternoon: on the walled approach the drag crushes Jaina (frost, nosebleed, crystal dimming); the horses shy and do not settle; she refuses to dismount; the walls end and Andorhal appears, working; 'The market gate.'
chapters.chronologyNotes: Chapter 6 continues Ch5's day 5 (the fork at first light). Arthas says the Garrow farm burned 'yesterday' (day 4). The sun is 'low' at the rise; the tally-man says he left Andorhal 'this noon'. The camp's rider arrives from the east at a canter as Arthas turns to leave. The party leaves the camp around or after midday and comes 'down out of the hills in the middle of the afternoon'; the exact distance from Strahnbrad to Andorhal is not stated. Not stated: how many days Arthas needs to quiet the hills.

chapters.timespan: Day 5, from the last of the low sun at the market gate through lamp-lighting to the night after the Exchange bell for the night shift (full dark); minutes before Chapter 8's capture.
keyEvents: Last of the low sun: the horses are left in a carter's yard outside the wall; the four enter Andorhal on foot on Sylvanas's Farstrider pass; the clerk records 'Proudmoore, Dalaran, Kirin Tor. Escort, Farstriders, three.' and Sylvanas's name; a barrel chalker keeps a second count

The militia post: Havel gives the street truth (Mill Lane sickness, the supplier change, loaders in pairs); Corin gives the paper truth (forty-one copied marks, Dalaran silent, the sample room); the lamplighter reaches the post; the work splits at the bench: Jaina, Corin and Lyriel to the sample room; Sylvanas, Cyndia and Havel to the granary district; rendezvous when the Exchange rings the night shift

Dusk to full dark in the granary district: Cyndia counts eight sentries at Fenner's yard; Sylvanas follows a runner (who drops something in a wall crack) by Tenter Row and a back lane over the roofs to Kett's loft and sees five masked men dress sacks from a crock; the Exchange bell sounds; the crews answer it

Night at the post: Jaina returns grey and frost-rimed with the sample-room verdict; the halves are laid side by side; Havel proposes a dawn arrest; Corin argues speed; Sylvanas orders 'Tonight.'; Jaina offers to freeze a man's jaw once; Cyndia, Lyriel, Havel's lads and Corin are placed; the candle is pinched out
chapters.chronologyNotes: Continues day 5 (Ch6's low sun at the crest); the stabling and the ride down are skipped. Havel says the day crews go off at the Exchange bell 'when it's full dark' and the lamplighter is already lighting lamps while it is still dusk; Sylvanas's roof watch runs to the bell and she reaches the post just after it. Kett's is lit and working although Havel said it shut at noon. Havel's account puts the supplier change at high summer and the first drilled loaders from midsummer; the barley man says he was at the gate 'yesterday'. The party reaches the post about the lamp-lighting hour. Chapter 8 opens minutes after the decision.
